facts.statement: Tecovasuchus is an extinct genus belonging to the aetosaur family.
facts.quote: Tecovasuchus is an extinct genus of aetosaur.

facts.statement: Before its formal description, fossils attributed to Tecovasuchus were previously classified as Paratypothorax or similar aetosaurs.
facts.quote: Before its description, specimens of Tecovasuchus were thought to belong to Paratypothorax or a Paratypothorax-like aetosaur.

facts.statement: Tecovasuchus is distinguished by osteoderms with thickened, beveled edges, deep pits, radiating grooves, and tongue-shaped dorsal flanges.
facts.quote: Several features of the osteoderms distinguish Tecovasuchus from other aetosaur genera, including dorsal paramedian osteoderms with strongly thickened and beveled posterior edges and ornamentation consisting of deep pits and radiating grooves, as well as tongue-shaped dorsal and plate-like ventrolateral flanges.

facts.statement: Fossils of Tecovasuchus are primarily found in the Late Triassic Tecovas Formation in Texas, dating to the lower Norian stage.
facts.quote: It is known primarily from osteoderms found from the Tecovas Formation in Texas, which is Late Triassic in age, dating back to the lower Norian.

facts.statement: Remains of Tecovasuchus have also been discovered in the Chinle Group in New Mexico and Arizona, ranging from Carnian to Rhaetian ages.
facts.quote: Material is also known from several other localities of the Chinle Group in New Mexico and Arizona, such as older Carnian outcrops and younger Rhaetian outcrops.

facts.statement: Specimens of Tecovasuchus have been collected from the Tecovas Formation, Bluewater Creek Formation, and the Los Esteros Member of the Santa Rosa Formation.
facts.quote: Specimens of Tecovasuchus have been collected from the Tecovas Formation, the Bluewater Creek Formation, and the Los Esteros Member of the Santa Rosa Formation.

facts.statement: Tecovasuchus serves as an index taxon for the St. Johnsian sub-LVF, helping correlate Late Triassic localities in the southwestern United States.
facts.quote: Tecovasuchus is an index taxon for the St. Johnsian sub-LVF (land vertebrate faunachron) of the Adamanian LVF, and the presence of material belonging to the genus helps correlate different Late Triassic localities throughout the southwestern United States.

facts.statement: Tecovasuchus belongs to the parent group Paratypothoracisini.
Tecovasuchus is classified within the family Stagonolepididae.
Tecovasuchus lived during the Norian stage, between 227.3 and 205.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Norian (227.3 to 205.7 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The genus was first recognized as a new taxon in 1995 but was formally named in 2006.
rejected.quote: Tecovasuchus was first recognized as a new taxon in 1995, although it was not named until the description of the type species, T. chatterjeei, in 2006.
